title: cost-optimization-autotune-defaults-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Aisha Patel
body: Motivation: reduce per-token unit economics for common production workloads by combining autotuned defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching with curated quantization profiles and a lightweight unit-economics (uecon) tooling surface. This PR introduces: 1) an autotune controller that adjusts default batching windows and cache policies based on observed latency/throughput tradeoffs, 2) new quantization profiles for gpt-family and llama-family variants (4-bit and 3-bit compatible presets) surfaced in the model registry, and 3) a UEcon CLI and Console dashboard tab that projects per-route token costs given runtime telemetry and recommended config changes. The description below is a single continuous string but includes conceptual sections for reviewers. Changeset summary: - Runtime: autotune controller (+metrics, safety caps) and updated default configs - Serving: KV prefix cache eviction heuristics and cooperative prefetching for hot prefixes - Quantization: add profiles and selection logic in model registry and runtime kernel selector - UEcon tooling: CLI that reads tracer/metrics and a Console UI page with what-if slider for batching/cache/quant settings - Tests and docs: unit + integration tests for controller; migration notes and Console docs Migration/compat: defaults are opt-in for existing dedicated/private deployments; hosted accounts will receive a staged rollout (canary) controlled by rollout policy. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for autotune heuristics - [x] Integration tests for cache behavior under load - [x] E2E for console UEcon page (smoke) - [x] Performance regression benchmarks (latency P50/P95) - [x] Docs + upgrade notes Implementation notes and safety: autotune respects per-customer latency SLOs and uses a short-term EWMA for decisioning; aggressive quant profiles are only suggested by the Console and require explicit model pinning. See release_notes and metrics below.

reviews: Marco Liu: Left a request for clearer SLO safety caps and fallback path in case autotune pushes latency above customer SLOs. Asked for unit tests that cover SLO breach simulation.

Aisha Patel (author): Responded that autotune uses per-tenant SLOs from config; added tests that simulate SLO breaches and added an immediate rollback flag. Also added a 'max_batch_ms' hard cap configurable via env.
Eva González: Requested more detail in docs on Dedicated/Private opt-in migration and a canary rollout plan for hosted. Asked to make quant suggestions explicit (not auto-applied).
Aisha Patel: Updated migration docs and Console copy to make quant suggestions require explicit pinning. Confirmed hosted rollout uses Canary tag and a 2-week gradual expansion policy.
Samir Reddy: Ran perf bench and requested a small optimization in prefix cache prefetch backoff to reduce extra GPU loads; included a follow-up commit to fix this.
Eva González: Approved after docs updates. Marco Liu: Approved after adding SLO tests. Samir Reddy: Approved.
ci_checks: benchmarks: perf-regression check - no regressions in P50/P95 observed in canary runs
merge: squash and merge by Marco Liu on 2026-02-18 - commit message: feat(autotune/uecon): default autotune for batching/caching + quant profiles + uecon tooling
release_notes: Introduces autotuned defaults for batching and prefix caching, curated quantization profiles (q3_k, q4_k) for common model families, and a UEcon estimate CLI + Console dashboard. Hosted rollout via canary; Dedicated/Private remain opt-in. Expected unit cost reduction: 8-25% depending on workload and model. See docs/migration/autotune-defaults.md for upgrade steps.
expected_impact_metrics: Unit cost reduction: 8-25% (median ~12% for batchable text-gen workloads)
Cache hit improvement: up to 18% for prefix-heavy chat workloads
